sourcedFrom: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) (2026)
cleanIntro: The .45 ACP full-size USP: hammer-fired, modified Browning linkless action, 4.41 inch polygonal barrel, 10- or 12-round magazines, and HK's patented recoil reduction system buried in the captive recoil assembly — the feature that was designed around the .45's recoil impulse in the first place. The strip is toolless and runs through the slide release axle. HK documents the USP45 in the USP SERIES book alongside the 9mm and .40 models; the procedures are common, the dimensions and the exploded-view parts list are its own.

steps.title: Confirm the model row and learn your variant
steps.action: This book covers the whole USP family; the Section 3 specification table carries the USP45 as its own column — .45 ACP, 10 & 12 round magazines, 4.41 inch barrel, 7.87 inches overall. Before touching the controls, work out which of the ten trigger/firing-mode variants your pistol is, because whether the frame lever is a safety, a decocker, both, or missing entirely is a parts question, not a model question.
steps.prose: A USP45 Variant 1 and a USP45 LEM strip identically but handle completely differently at the lever. Every later step that says 'decock' or 'SAFE' means: as your variant provides.
steps.quote: The USP is available in both full-size frame, compact models, as well as specialized models, with ten trigger/firing mode configurations and three calibers—.45 ACP, .40 S&W, 9mm (special order on some models).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 1 — INTRODUCTION, p.6

steps.title: No lever tells you it is safe — only the empty chamber does
steps.action: Muzzle safe, finger outside the guard, and treat the pistol as loaded and ready to fire until the magazine is out and you have confirmed the chamber empty by eye and by finger. Your USP45 may be a variant with no conventional manual safety at all.
steps.prose: HK leads the manual with this because the USP's variant system means two outwardly identical pistols can differ in exactly the control you were about to trust.
steps.quote: Like most modern handguns, the HK USP pistol may be equipped in a configuration that does not have a conventional manual safety. Therefore, you must consider it to be loaded and ready to fire until you have removed the magazine and visually and physically (with your finger) confirmed that the chamber is empty.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Cover page
steps.warn: A chambered round fires when the trigger is pressed whether or not a magazine is fitted, on every variant without a magazine disconnect.

steps.title: Paddle catch, hand under the magazine, magazine out
steps.action: Put the support hand under the floorplate, press the ambidextrous paddle magazine catch at the back of the trigger guard, and withdraw the magazine. A loaded .45 magazine is heavy enough to dent whatever it lands on, which is what the hand underneath is for.
steps.prose: Magazine first, always — the slide stays shut until the ammunition supply is out of the gun.
steps.quote: 2. Remove the magazine. 1. Hold your hand under the magazine. 2. Press paddle magazine catch (Fig. 9-A) 3. Remove magazine (Fig. 10-B).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 5 — CLEARING AND SAFETY CHECK PROCEDURE, p.25

steps.title: Rack, lock back, and watch what leaves the port
steps.action: Grip the rear serrations, rack the slide fully to the rear with the muzzle safe, push up and hold the slide release, and ease the slide forward until it locks open. Keep your eyes on the ejection port through the stroke: if a round was chambered it comes out here, and you want to see it go.
steps.prose: A .45 case is big enough that not seeing anything eject is itself information — but the book still sends you to the chamber check next, because absence of evidence is not an empty chamber.
steps.quote: 3. Open and lock the slide to the rear. Grasping the rear serrations, rack the slide to the rear while keeping the muzzle pointed in a safe direction (A). Push and hold upwards on the slide release (B) and lock the slide to the rear by allowing the slide to move forward until it engages the slide release. Watch for a cartridge or empty case to be ejected out through the ejection port.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 5 — CLEARING AND SAFETY CHECK PROCEDURE, p.25

steps.title: Look in the chamber, then put a finger in it
steps.action: Visually inspect the chamber through the open port, then insert a finger through the port and sweep both the chamber mouth and the feed ramp. Clear out anything found. A cartridge that stays after repeating the procedure goes to a gunsmith — never to a pocketknife.
steps.prose: The finger sweep exists because the visual check has a blind spot exactly where a half-fed round rests against the ramp.
steps.quote: 4. Inspect the chamber. Inspect the chamber for the presence of a cartridge or empty case by: 1. Visually inspecting the chamber through the open ejection port. 2. Physically inserting a finger through the ejection port and sweeping the chamber and feed ramp area. 3. Removing any cartridges or empty cases from the chamber or from within the USP. 4. If the cartridge remains in the chamber, repeat the Clearing Procedure. If the cartridge will not extract, contact a gunsmith.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 5 — CLEARING AND SAFETY CHECK PROCEDURE, p.25

steps.title: Set the slide to the disassembly position
steps.action: Drop the slide off the lock, then hold the pistol with your thumb over the rear of the frame and fingers on top of the slide. Draw the slide rearward just far enough that the retention tab of the slide release appears in the recess on the left side of the slide, and hold that alignment.
steps.prose: There is no detent holding this position — your firing hand is the fixture. If your grip creeps, the axle binds, and the correct response is to re-find the recess, not to lever at the release.
steps.quote: 4. Using the firing hand, pull the slide back to the rear so that the retention tab of the slide release is visible through the recess on the left side of the slide (see Fig. 13).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.27

steps.title: Slide release out: press the axle from the right
steps.action: With the free hand, press the slide release axle in from the right side of the frame and draw the release completely out of the left side. On a USP45 that has seen service the axle can be snug; steady thumb pressure beats any tool, and the moment the alignment is right it gives.
steps.prose: This one lever is the entire takedown mechanism — there is no rotating lever, no takedown pins. Respect what that means in reverse too: reassembly ends by putting it back in the same alignment.
steps.quote: 5. With the non-firing hand, press on the axle of the slide release from the right side of the frame, and completely remove the slide release from the left side of the frame.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.27

steps.title: Upper off the frame — keep the recoil assembly captive
steps.action: Run the slide, barrel and recoil spring assembly forward off the frame rails as one unit, with a hand cupped under the open bottom of the slide. The recoil assembly is under tension until it is deliberately unseated, and HK's warning is blunt: uncontrolled, it can injure you or get damaged or lost.
steps.prose: The .45's recoil reduction assembly is the heaviest spring package in the USP line — treat it like the loaded spring it is.
steps.quote: Hold the recoil assembly in place while rem­ ovi­ng the slide from the frame. If not, this assembly could be released under spring tens­ ion and could possibly cause injury to pers­ on­nel, or become dama­ ged or lost.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.27
steps.warn: Spring under tension — keep it seated until you mean to release it.

steps.title: Recoil assembly out sideways, then barrel out through the port
steps.action: Slide upside down: push the captive recoil spring assembly forward, then up and out to the left or right, clear of barrel and slide. It stays assembled — HK does not recommend taking the captive unit apart. Then pivot the barrel slightly forward, press up on it through the ejection port, and lift it free.
steps.prose: Forward-then-sideways is what unhooks the guide rod's rear seat from the barrel locking block without a fight. Straight up just cocks it in the slide.
steps.quote:
7. Turn the slide upside down and carefully push the recoil spring forward, up, and out
to either the left or right side, separating the recoil spring from the barrel and slide (see Figure 15). The USP series pistols use a “captive” recoil spring assembly, disa­ s­sem­bly is not recommended. 8. Pivot the barrel slightly forward and press upward on the barrel through the ejection port, separating the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.28

steps.title: ⛔ The bore is polygonal — bronze bristles, never steel
steps.action: Scrub the bore with a solvent-wet bronze brush, six passes minimum chamber to muzzle, then patch it out. A steel brush scratches the polygonal profile and permanently costs accuracy — the .45's big bore makes the polygon easy to inspect with a light, and it should look like a mirror with rounded flats, not a scratched tube.
steps.prose: Polygonal rifling is why USP bores clean fast: less surface for fouling to key into. Let that work for you instead of scrubbing harder with the wrong brush.
steps.quote: Do not use a steel bore brush which can scratch the polygonal bore and reduce accuracy.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 8 — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, p.41

steps.title: Field strip complete at four groups — the armorer line
steps.action: Slide, barrel, captive recoil assembly, frame: that is the entire user disassembly. HK draws the line right there — further disassembly is certified-armorer work — and the intervals to run this strip are Normal cleaning after each firing or every twelve months, Major cleaning after 600 cartridges or after sand, dust or water exposure.
steps.prose: The USP45's variant internals (sear, hammer, catch, control lever parts) are modular, which tempts tinkering; modular for an armorer with the parts chart is not modular for a bench with a pin punch.
steps.quote: Disassembly of the pistol is now comp­ lete. Only an HK certified armorer should disassemble the pistol further.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.28

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Ammunition: brass-cased factory spec only, +P+ barred
deepSteps.action: The USP45 runs brass-cased factory ammunition to NATO, SAAMI or CIP spec. The book prohibits +P+ (a marking with no defined pressure standard), reloads, remanufactured, steel-cased, aluminum-cased and handloads, and further bars military surplus, corrosive-primed, cast-lead and submachine-gun-loaded cartridges. The recoil reduction system tolerates +P; it does not license anything past it.
deepSteps.prose: .45 ACP is a low-pressure cartridge with a lot of +P lore around it. The line HK actually draws is the +P+ marking and non-factory ammunition — everything on the barred list has either an undefined pressure or an undefined history.
deepSteps.quote: USP pistols are designed to fire quality, brass-cased, factory-loaded ammunition loaded to NATO, SAAMI (Sporting Arms and Ammunition Manufacturers’ Institute), or CIP (Permanent International Commission for the Proof of Small Arms) specifications for use, specifically in handguns. DO NOT USE “+P+”, reloaded, remanufactured, steel cased, aluminum cased, or handloaded ammunition because it may not meet applicable NATO, SAAMI or CIP standards and could cause death, serious personal injury, and/or damage to your pistol and may void your warranty.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 5 — AMMUNITION, p.17

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The hammer never gets lowered by hand on a live chamber
deepSteps.action: Decocking is the lever's job on variants that have it. Lowering the hammer manually with the trigger pulled drops it past the half-cock notch and bypasses the passive safeties — and on DA/SA variants without a decock function, HK states it is unsafe to lower the hammer on a chambered round at all. The manual's hand-lowering procedure exists only for Variant 9/10 pistols on a VERIFIED EMPTY chamber.
deepSteps.prose: Half the negligent discharges this manual is defending against live in this one habit imported from other hammer guns. The USP's answer is mechanical: use the decocker or leave the hammer alone.
deepSteps.quote: Any attempt to lower the hammer manually (with a round in the chamber), will allow the hammer to be lowered past the half-cock notch and by­passes the passive safeties which are built into the USP and could result in an acc­ i­den­tal disc­ harge and subsequent property damage, injury or loss of life.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 5 — LOADING, p.19

deepSteps.title: Magazine apart: detent, controlled spring, floorplate forward
deepSteps.action: On the 12-round magazine: depress the locking detent in the floorplate with a blunt pointed instrument, hold it, cover the magazine base with a hand, and slide the floorplate forward off. Ease the locking plate and spring out gradually, then remove plate, spring and follower. The 10-round pattern adds squeezing the floorplate locking tabs on both sides while the detent is held.
deepSteps.prose: Which pattern you own decides the third hand you wish you had — read the floorplate before pressing anything.
deepSteps.quote: 4. Gradually allow the lock­ing plate and magazine spring to expand out of the magazine housing.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 6 — MAGAZINE DISASSEMBLY, p.35
deepSteps.warn: Magazine base away from face and eyes; the spring is stacked to full compression.

deepSteps.title: Major cleaning: 600 rounds, magazines apart, parts immersed
deepSteps.action: At 600 cartridges — or after sand, dust or water, saltwater above all — escalate to Major cleaning: everything from the normal routine, plus the magazine disassembled for cleaning, plus all parts rinsed or immersed in cleaning solution and scrubbed with a nylon brush, then dried fully with compressed air or rag and swabs before lubrication.
deepSteps.prose: The .45 throws proportionally more unburned powder than the 9mm at the same round count; the 600 number is the same, so do not stretch it because the gun 'still looks clean' outside.
deepSteps.caution: Ultrasonic baths strip the colored reference markings from frame, extractor and control lever — normally unnecessary under standard ammunition.
deepSteps.quote: Major Cleaning - Major Cleaning is the same as normal cleaning except that: • The magazine is disassembled for cleaning, following the instructions in Section 6. • All parts should be rinsed with or immersed in cleaning solution and thoroughly scrubbed with a nylon brush. The parts can be dried using compressed air or with a rag and cotton swabs.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 8 — Major Cleaning, p.43

deepSteps.title: ⛔ No alterations — and the 2005 hammer/catch revision trap
deepSteps.action: Do not alter any part of the pistol or magazine, including 'improvements' — the warranty and the safety case both die with the first modified part. USP-specific: the catch was revised in 2005 to match a revised hammer, the old and new parts function only in matched sets, and a mismatch creates a genuine safety issue. Hammer-group work is armorer work with part numbers verified.
deepSteps.prose: The two catch generations are near-twins to the eye. HK prints them side by side in the manual precisely because eyeballing has already failed people.
deepSteps.quote: Do not alter any of the parts or components of the pistol or magazine, e.g., do not attempt to “improve” or make the pistol “better” by altering parts or components. Altering any parts or components of the pistol or magazine may cause serious injury or death, damage to the pistol, or other damage to property, and voids its warranty.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 8 — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, p.41

deepSteps.title: Lock-Out Device in the grip — and the slide it freezes
deepSteps.action: Post-October-1999 USPs carry the internal Lock-Out Device in the lanyard-loop insert, worked by its two-pronged key through the magazine well: clockwise to lock, holes horizontal when locked, and the trigger, hammer AND slide are all frozen. Clear the pistol before locking it, and on LEM variants dry fire once first to release the hammer spring or the lock will not engage.
deepSteps.prose: A locked USP whose slide will not open is behaving correctly. Check the lock-plate holes before assuming a mechanical failure.
deepSteps.caution: Never force the slide on a locked pistol.
deepSteps.quote: The HK Lock-Out Device is not a substitute for safe gun handling practices. Never point the muzzle of the pistol in an unsafe direction (at yourself or others). When the Lock-Out Device is placed in the locked position the slide is locked in the closed position and cannot be moved!
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — USP SERIES — Covering USP, USP Compact, and USP Specialized Models — June 2026 (imprint page) — Section 10 — LOCK-OUT DEVICE, p.46

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Nylon toothbrush with cleaning solution over all internal surfaces
Rag and cotton swabs to lift the loosened fouling, breech face included

cleaning.name: BARREL AND LOCKING BLOCK
tasks: Bronze bore brush, solvent, six passes chamber to muzzle — steel is banned on the polygonal bore
Patches until clean, then toothbrush over the barrel exterior and locking block

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING ASSEMBLY AND FRAME
tasks: Wipe and brush the captive recoil assembly clean — never disassemble it
Scrub carbon off the frame, concentrating under the slide and around the unlock block that meets the barrel

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Brush the follower and feed lips clean at every Normal cleaning
Full disassembly of the magazine only at Major cleaning
Confirm the follower runs free and rises nearly flush to the feed lips after reassembly

cleaning.name: INTERVALS AND LUBRICATION
tasks: Normal cleaning after each firing or every twelve months
Major cleaning after 600 cartridges or any sand/dust/water exposure
Light lube on barrel exterior and all metal; medium lube on locking block, rails, controls, extractor and sear; none on plastic, rubber or ammunition

reassembly: Set the barrel into the slide — muzzle in the front hole, locking block in the ejection port, angled locking surfaces showing along the slide's underside.
Seat the front of the recoil spring guide rod in the small hole in the front of the slide.
Align the guide rod's rear angled surfaces with the barrel locking block's, push the assembly forward, and engage the recoil spring retainer on the shelf at the front of the locking block.
Thumb the recoil assembly seated; confirm the sear axle is flush with both sides of the frame.
Offer the rear of the slide over the front of the frame and draw it back, pressing the disconnector down so the frame inserts enter the slide grooves.
Retract to put the left-side recess over the axle hole, hold, and push the slide release in from the left until flush.
Clear the pistol and run the function check printed for YOUR variant — the book carries five.
fncheck: Clear the USP45, rack the slide briskly three or four times and feel for binding — there should be none. Then the variant check: safety variants must hold the hammer on SAFE and drop it on FIRE; DA/SA variants must catch the sear with an audible click when the slide is cycled with the trigger held, then fire again single-action after the reset; decocker variants must drop the hammer safely to the catch, never to the firing pin; LEM and V7 guns run the double-action cycle and reset. Finish on an empty magazine: the slide must lock back when racked.
